Decompose prompt bellow with actions , dependencies, implication using "implicature resolvers principles" classifying and producing an output that we will use into a "miadiRun" later
<prompt>
You will be a sub-agent. Not necessarily a sub-agent, but we're starting your session as if you were a sub-agent. Responsible for mapping. You have 114 repositories connected. And you're running in the cloud. And we will be interested in creating a relational mapping of these repository, but not as you usually understand the term relational.
let's say first what it is not.
* It's not relational database.
* It has nothing to do with Western or European culture, which most of your training data comes from. Therefore, you can assume automatically that any output you produce is biased and need revision.
* We are not in a linear way of thinking, but in a cyclical one. And you'll understand that by looking at  our the repository jgwill/medicine-wheel and installing the relevant packages where your repository mapping will live.
Okay, I agree it's not just what it is not, it contains insight into what might happen.
Here is what I don't know that might help:
*! I have no idea if... There are existing definitions that are really recent. We need to be really careful about not being affected by past hallucination, which many of these repositories were done with ancient model that were much less intelligent than you are. And given the fact that they are much more intelligent model than you are, you'll need to limit yourself and what you will work. And what I don't know here is, do I have a recent definition of what a prototype is about? We don't need extensive definition about that, but I know that this is now possible to actually associate with an episode, an actual prototype public URL, as well as its editing URL, which implies opening the agent session that is actually implementing and is capable to use, for instance, a Chrome browser to actually steer that model and evolve the prototype, or to pull the changes in there and publish a new version of the prototype. And either way, many of the repositories that you have are actually prototype, I would say at least 25%. Therefore, there's a cycle of what a prototype is, and one of the recent one is the author's desk. Which is one of the most important one. Another one, which I love, that is pretty old, but it has really something interesting. It was a Copilot workspace that I tried to recreate when the GitHub team retired. And I know that inside of the factory, we are trying at one level for one of the team that is there. We're trying to have a similar chain of events to arrive at something like that. So I know that this prototype is going to be important as well.
    •    I don't know what's the best way to actually decide where to put this mapping. What I know is, personally speaking, all of the repositories that are there are either they're mine directly, they are ones of my agents, or there are forks that we did from contributors from the community. Therefore, if I had to say this is really important for me to achieve a goal of being credible online for my career, I wouldn't judge in the mess that is in there, but I would definitely want inside of each of these repositories something that give us a statement of what it is. Otherwise, I would want a minimum amount of repositories to at least have a mapping of these. One of my thinking in that regard would be  using repositories like <owner>/<owner> (ex. miadisabelle/miadisabelle, avadisabelle/avadisabelle, jgwill/jgwill, …) to actually store these mapping. And I think that  "jgwill/jgwill" could be one of the hub that relates to others, as this would become an agentic platform or something. And there's another one that is my personal account, which basically is probably the one, you know, I'm thinking of a job posting, and they ask that you give your GitHub username so they arrive inside of your profile, which I'm not going to give jgwill/jgwill but repo guillaumedescoteauxisabelle/guillaumedescoteauxisabelle
    •    I know that putting this mapping inside of markdown files that we can't process with any CLI or any application is something completely useless. We'll need to be capable of interpreting the minimal amount of columns and try to understand the position of each of these repositories in terms of what they did, what they might do in the future, in which academic fields do they locate, and where are they type prototype, or they are more something that we actually distribute and maintain actively, which by looking at the Git log of each of them, you'll be capable of knowing about that. All of that aspect should enable you to actually decompose into the most meaningful data structure and create us the most basic CLI and small server that we could start. You know, you are inside s ok something like .miadi/repository-mapping/ (for any of <owner>/<owner> , ex.  miadisabelle/miadisabelle/.miadi/repository-mapping/)) and there are structured JSONL the when you start the CLI and Web UI we are capable to know some really basic information about the mapping you did and navigate to them. jgwill/jgwill/.miadi/repository-mapping/ would have a little bit more structure, because it would be capable of mapping and consume all other mapping. It means maybe it's called a meta mapping or something, which basically you don't map and index all of the repositories of others there, but you consume the data from their repositories if that exists. So it's a way to register other owners from there, which I think is going to work.
    •    repository "jgwill/smcraft" is one of a tool where we experimented creating system diagrams, which contain three other type of diagrams, such as the entity relationship diagram ( There might be some contradiction with the actual initial definition that I gave you about relational, but we are making it relational. For instance, relational to the state machine diagram and the events, as well as the sequence diagram that are currently being supported there. So if you need a way to actually define the schema of what you're going to create, definitely these will help you create the most appropriate representation of this little data structure that I'm talking about, probably with the entity relationship diagram. And in terms of the state machine, I think that there's a little very simple state machine, like when a repository is in a state of being a prototype, there's an event that makes it transition what we explored into a concrete implementation. So it's just, you know, these are going to be something that you will save as little specifications, you know, very simple, like, okay, I've been asked to write specifications for a feature. I must define that feature in less than 55 words. So you'll need to be careful here that when you are trying to define a feature in more than 55 words, you need to self-correct and stop there and move to the next feature. And if there's something that you could do is actually put a status for each of the features that you're discovering, and you can mark it as unclear or undefinable or needs resolution or something like that. Because sometimes when you are going to do the mapping, you're going to try to name the three core feature that you're observing inside of a repository if you decided that this is a prototype. And obviously with some semantics, you're going to try to relate a repository with another one.
    •    repository "jgwill/medicine-wheel" contain a service that we are actually using and deploying. And I know that right now it supports infrastructure inventory, which basically is a registry of everything that runs on a machine. And my feeling is everything that you're doing is part of a need to have repository inventory or something. So there would be in there in its own  a subfolder "./rispecs/developer-suite/repository-mapping/<RISE framework specs (see repo "jgwill/llms-txt") >/<here>.spec.md … (which basically corresponds to what I am asking you todo in this complex work.  Probably the Cli And small Web UI helpers for the .miadi/repository-mapping I am asking can be there or into repository "jgwill/Miadi" (subfolder "./packages/<main package name you are designing>/" (ex. @miadi/relational-repository-mapper and we would consume the @medicine-wheel/developer-repository-mapping package you are creating todo your whole work.
    •    repository branch (PR) subfolder "./rispecs/developer-suite/repository-mapping/<RISE framework specs (see repo "jgwill/llms-txt") >/<here>.erdf.json (all diagrams from stateloom (jgwill/smcraft) can also be there.
    •    Also extend "jgwill/medicine-wheel" with another layer of inventory for "platform-features/capabilities" so that all the "repository-mapping I am asking will consume that data-structure for true relational database (there the relationality of my early vocabulary on "relational" is meaning the same, the @medicine-wheel/ontology-core should contain these realities as you are experimenting a "researchIsCeremony" and are part of what is implied in the IAIP platform developped into repo "miadisabelle/Etuaptmumk-RSM" (./sources/researchIsCeremony/ contains Theoretical Framework from private repository for referencing your decision as you design your different layers )
</prompt>

ambiguities.text: [implicature:manner] 'Not a relational database' conflicts with 'true relational database' for the capabilities layer, which the prompt itself notices
ambiguities.suggestion: Name two senses: relational (kinship and accountability edges) and entity-relationship (the ERD schema). The ERD stores the edges, and each edge carries the first meaning.

ambiguities.text: The CLI and web UI could live in jgwill/medicine-wheel or in jgwill/Miadi packages/ as @miadi/relational-repository-mapper
ambiguities.suggestion: Keep the data package in medicine-wheel (@medicine-wheel/developer-repository-mapping) and put the CLI and UI in jgwill/Miadi as its consumer, as the prompt's example shows.

ambiguities.text: [implicature:quantity] An identity statement inside each repository versus a minimum of owner-level mappings
ambiguities.suggestion: Start with owner-level mappings. Propose per-repository statements as a list for consent, because it means writing into 114 repositories.

ambiguities.text: 'Limit yourself' because more capable models exist does not name a bound
ambiguities.suggestion: Bound by evidence-only claims, three features per prototype, 55 words per feature, and status flags instead of speculation.

ambiguities.text: [presupposition] A recent prototype definition may or may not exist, and its location is unknown
ambiguities.suggestion: Search chronicle episodes, jgwill/miadi-orchestration-kit and QMD first. Write a short definition only if none exists, and record that it is new.

ambiguities.text: ontology-core 'should contain these realities' but the NodeType union is closed at eight
ambiguities.suggestion: Use knowledge nodes with metadata.kind 'repository' and 'capability'. A new NodeType needs its own ontology revision issue.

ambiguities.text: 'Minimal amount of columns' is not listed
ambiguities.suggestion: Propose: id, owner, name, fork_of, lifecycle_state, last_commit, commit_cadence, purpose_past, direction_future, academic_fields, features[], relations[], evidence, review_status.

ambiguities.text: researchIsCeremony sits in a private source
